pages.html:
For Larry and any designated GRIT editor. Use this checklist to turn submissions into an edited issue, give the layout assistant a complete package, and get the finished issue through approval. Start by confirming the issue month in the submissions app.

You can manage the editorial work without learning Adobe InDesign. The layout assistant prepares the page layout; use the GRIT Layout Monthly Guide if you are doing that work yourself. For publication rules, use the approved content rules and submission guide.

The route from submission to finished issue

Submissions app → issue plan → copied Google Docs editing template → reviewed Markdown file and image/ad files in Google Drive → layout assistant → PDF review and approval → office distribution.

Markdown is a plain-text file with simple formatting markers, such as # before an article title. You will use the template to turn it into a readable Google document for editing, then provide a checked .md file to the layout assistant. Image references in the text do not contain the actual images.

1. Have your access and issue folder ready

  1. Use the approved GRIT browser profile and accounts supplied during editor onboarding. Confirm that you can open the GRIT submissions app and its editor area, the GRIT Google Drive, the office's OneDrive workspace, and the existing layout contract/messages in Upwork.
  2. Ask the SHHA office or current editor to arrange missing access. Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive are separate services and may use different accounts. Do not assume your personal account has access. Keep passwords and account recovery details out of issue documents and messages.
  3. In Google Drive, choose My Drive, then open Monthly Issues → [year] → [issue folder]. Recent files can be convenient, but My Drive makes it easier to confirm where a file belongs.
  4. Create or confirm the current issue folder, with Ads and Images subfolders. Name the issue clearly, including both months for a combined issue. Keep the editing document, current Markdown file, and layout/proof versions together in this issue folder.

For help with sign-in or unfamiliar permission prompts, use Quick Links & Directory to find IT help. Access to this public procedure does not grant access to the working files.

2. Plan the correct issue

  1. Open the editor area of the submissions app and choose Issue Planning. Check the selected issue month before making changes. The default advances at the start of a month; use the issue selector when you are still finishing an earlier issue. Confirm which plan represents a combined issue.
  2. Review new submissions and the backlog. Use the Inbox to read a full submission when needed. Use Plan to bring an item into the selected issue.
  3. In Content Flow, put the selected items in the intended reading order. Review dates, titles, author bylines, relevance, and available space. A submission's private contact information is not automatically part of its published byline.
  4. Use placeholders to track expected material, such as a President's note or Board report. Follow up on missing material, then replace or remove the placeholders before sending the issue to layout.
  5. Agree the space budget with the layout assistant. Shorten, defer, or request revisions where needed, following the approved editorial rules and contributor-review requirements. Review deferred items again for a later issue.

The normal submission deadline is around the 20th for the following month's issue; confirm the current production dates and any combined-issue arrangements with the office and layout assistant. See the production schedule and responsibilities.

Planning figures need confirmation: the walkthrough mentioned approximately 3,500 words for a 16-page plan and 4,700 for an 18-page plan. These are working estimates, not submission limits or approved print specifications. Ads and images change the available space. The layout guide requires a final booklet page count divisible by four; clarify how planning pages and covers are counted before using the 18-page figure.

3. Collect the actual ads, photographs, and recurring material

The working layout package is in Google Drive. The office supplies current advertisements through OneDrive; copying files between them is a manual step in this workflow.

  1. Check with the office for the current ads, normally provided by the 20th. In OneDrive, open My files → GRIT Editor Workspace → Monthly Issues → [year] → [issue] → Ads, or the equivalent shared committee workspace supplied by the office.
  2. Download the current Ads folder. A folder download may arrive as a ZIP file in your computer's Downloads folder. Extract it and upload the actual ad files into the current Google Drive issue's Ads folder. Confirm the files open and belong to the current issue.
  3. Download the actual photographs and graphics supplied with selected submissions or by email, and upload them into Images. Copying submission text alone does not bring its attachments with it.
  4. For an article carried over from a previous issue, locate its matching artwork and copy it into the current issue. Preserve the earlier issue's archive.
  5. For recurring material such as Kids Corner, find the correct file for this issue or combined period. A list view can make full filenames easier to read. Use Make a copy and move the copy into the issue folder, leaving the reusable source intact. The GRIT Design Assets folder is another source of reusable artwork.

Check that every image works in black and white and has enough detail for print. Optional AI-generated illustrations need the same editorial review: check the subject, local details, odd objects or anatomy, contrast, and background before including them. An illustration does not establish that an article's claims are correct.

4. Copy the planned text into the Google Docs editing template

  1. In the submissions app, open Newsletter Preview. Check the article order and word count, then choose Copy Text. This copies the issue as simplified Markdown.
  2. In the GRIT Google Drive, find Master Template Content Editing. Make a copy, rename it for the issue, and move the copy into the current issue folder. Work in the copy so the master stays ready for the next issue.
  3. Open the copied Google document and wait for the custom GRIT menu to appear. Choose GRIT → Open Markdown Sidebar.
  4. On first use, the template may request Google authorization for GRIT Markdown Applier. Use only the approved template and intended account. If the script, requested access, or warning is unfamiliar, ask the current template maintainer or IT help to review it before continuing.
  5. Paste the copied text into the sidebar. Put the cursor in the blank working document and select Insert at cursor. You should see readable article text with styled headings.

The sidebar may clear if the page refreshes; text already inserted into the Google document remains saved. Check the document before inserting again, so you do not accidentally duplicate the whole issue.

5. Edit the document and identify images clearly

  1. Read the issue from beginning to end. Correct spelling, clarity, dates, links, titles, and bylines. Replace any “Untitled submission” heading with an appropriate title.
  2. Keep article titles as Heading 1, bylines as Heading 2, and ordinary text as normal paragraphs. This is an editing document; the layout assistant will handle the final page design.
  3. Remove unresolved placeholders. Where substantial revisions need the contributor's review, follow the approved editing and contributor-review rules.
  4. Identify each intended image with its exact filename in the text, plus any caption and placement note. For example: [PHOTO: fence-illustration.png], followed by “Place with the fence article; caption: …”. Confirm that the named file exists in the issue's Images folder.
  5. Keep the actual image files separate for layout. A vague note such as “put a picture here,” or a picture pasted only into the editing document, is not a complete image handoff. If you rename a file, update its text reference too.

6. Export and check the Markdown file

  1. Use Download Markdown in the GRIT sidebar to obtain a .md file. The download goes to your computer, usually Downloads; it does not automatically appear in Google Drive.
  2. Open that file in a plain-text editor and compare it with the reviewed Google document. Check a recent correction, the article order, titles, bylines, and image filenames. Confirm that your final edits are actually included.
  3. If the file contains the earlier, unedited text, ask the template maintainer for the approved way to export the edited document. The walkthrough did not establish whether the sidebar exports subsequent document edits or its original input. Resolve a mismatch before handing off the file.
  4. In Google Drive, open the current issue folder and choose New → File upload to upload the checked Markdown file. Give it a clear issue/version name and identify which file is current. After later editorial changes, export, check, and upload again.

7. Hand the complete package to the layout assistant

Before sending the handoff, confirm:

  • The issue month or combined period is correct.
  • Selected articles are edited, ordered, and have usable titles and bylines; placeholders are resolved.
  • The word/page budget and requested return date are agreed.
  • Current ads and every referenced image are present, open correctly, and have clear filenames.
  • The uploaded Markdown matches the reviewed document, and the current version is unambiguous.
  • The designated layout assistant can open the assigned issue folder through the approved sharing arrangement.

Use the existing contract's Upwork → Messages conversation. The walkthrough used Ashish as the layout assistant; confirm the current assignment. Give a new assistant access through the approved process, and agree the actual turnaround instead of assuming a previous issue's response time.

You can adapt this message:

Hello [name], I am the editor for the [month/year or combined period] GRIT. The layout package is ready at [Google Drive issue-folder link]. Please use [exact Markdown filename/version]. Current ads are in Ads and article images are in Images; the text identifies image filenames and captions. Please note [placement notes or explicitly identified outstanding items]. Can you return the first PDF by [agreed date/time and time zone]? Please let me know if any file or access is missing.

Keep editorial changes after handoff coordinated: tell the assistant exactly which file or passage has changed, so an older draft is not laid out by mistake.

8. Review the PDF and complete approval

The walkthrough focused on preparing and handing off the editorial package. The approval sequence below follows the existing GRIT Internal Production Reference.

  1. Review the returned PDF against the approved text and assets: article completeness, bylines, dates, links, captions, matching images, current ads, and readable black-and-white output. Send clear corrections to the layout assistant and check the revised PDF.
  2. Send the current Google Drive final-PDF link to the Board/Secretary for content review, copying the printer so the printer can prepare a proof in parallel. Ensure recipients can open the linked file.
  3. Obtain the Secretary's content approval. The office reviews and approves the printer proof after this content approval.
  4. If content changes during review, hold office proof approval. Have the PDF corrected and the printer prepare a new proof; only approve the proof of the corrected content version.
  5. Coordinate print distribution, email distribution, and online posting with the office. Keep the approved PDF and final source package clearly identified. Confirm the office's required OneDrive archive destination and copy the completed package there; do not assume the Google Drive working folder synchronizes automatically.

If something is missing or looks wrong

What you seeWhat to check next
The planned articles seem to have disappeared.Check the selected issue month; the default may have advanced.
A downloaded Markdown file is missing from Google Drive.Look in your computer's Downloads folder, verify the file, then upload it to the issue folder.
A recent Google Docs correction is missing from the Markdown.Compare the export with the document and ask the template maintainer to resolve the export method before layout.
The assistant cannot find an image.Check that the actual file is uploaded and that its filename exactly matches the text reference.
The GRIT menu does not appear.Wait for the copied template to load, then confirm you copied the script-enabled Master Template Content Editing document. Ask the maintainer if it still does not appear.
Sign-in, authorization, or file sharing fails.Confirm the intended GRIT account and ask the office/current editor or IT help to check access. Do not change organization security settings to get around the prompt.

Prepared from the October 16, 2026 editor walkthrough. The word/page estimates and edited-document Markdown export behavior are verification checkpoints, not new publication policy.

Operational reference for office staff, IT admin, and future volunteers — mailing lists, shared mailboxes, licensing, SOPs, and governance.

Quick Overview

SHHA uses two different patterns for email collaboration:

PatternTechnologyExamples
Committee mailing lists Microsoft Groups shha-all@, csc@, acc@
Role-based addresses Shared mailboxes president@, cscchair@, accchair@

Design Principles

  • Role continuity over individual ownership — email addresses stay constant when people rotate in/out.
  • Least cost for volunteers — external volunteers do not require paid M365 licenses.
  • Operational traceability — group membership changes trigger Power Automate notifications.
  • Institutional archive — admin@ is included in all groups as a permanent archive recipient.

Microsoft Groups (Mailing Lists)

Each committee has a Microsoft Group that acts as its mailing list.

GroupAddress
All membersshha-all@sandiahomeowners.org
CSCcsc@sandiahomeowners.org
ACCacc@sandiahomeowners.org
OthersOne group per committee

Behavior: Sending to the group distributes to all members. Membership is maintained by staff (primary owner: Anna). External participants can be included.

Shared Mailboxes (Role Inboxes)

Only six officer role addresses are shared mailboxes tied to positions, not people: President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, ACC Chair, and CSC Chair. Other committee chairs and task-force leads use their own account and the committee mailing list.

RoleAddress
CSC Chaircscchair@sandiahomeowners.org
ACC Chairaccchair@sandiahomeowners.org
Presidentpresident@sandiahomeowners.org
Vice Presidentvicepresident@sandiahomeowners.org
Secretarysecretary@sandiahomeowners.org
Treasurertreasurer@sandiahomeowners.org

Each incoming officer receives both Full Access and Send As permission through the officer's own licensed SHHA account. Officers cannot log in directly to the shared mailbox and must add it manually in Outlook because it may not appear automatically. For official role correspondence, send from the role mailbox or copy it so the shared mailbox remains the archive.

Access model

  • People do not log in directly as the role mailbox.
  • Authorized users open the shared mailbox from their own licensed account.
  • Example: phil.krehbiel@sandiahomeowners.org can open accchair@sandiahomeowners.org.

When leadership changes

  1. Remove predecessor access.
  2. Grant successor access.
  3. Keep the role mailbox address unchanged.

Archive Mailbox (admin@)

  • admin@ is a member of all groups.
  • Purpose: permanent archive and continuity.
  • admin@ is not actively monitored for normal operations.

Power Automate Membership Notifications

A Power Automate flow sends email notifications whenever group membership changes.

  • Provides audit visibility.
  • Alerts staff to unexpected changes.
  • Supports handoffs and troubleshooting.

Licensing and External Volunteers

User typeLicense needed?Capabilities
External volunteersNoGroup email delivery, SharePoint guest access
Licensed staff / adminYes (paid M365)Group administration, shared mailbox access, full portal

Responsibilities Matrix

ResponsibilityPrimaryBackupNotes
Maintain committee group membershipAnna (staff)IT adminAdd/remove members, verify accuracy
Manage shared mailbox permissionsAnna + IT adminIT adminRemove predecessor, add successor
Ensure admin@ in all groupsIT adminAnnaRequired for archive continuity
Monitor membership-change notificationsAnnaIT adminPower Automate emails = operational signal
Troubleshoot delivery/access issuesIT adminAnnaIncludes mailbox permissions and group settings

SOP: Add a Person to a Committee Mailing List

  1. Confirm committee and target group address.
  2. Verify whether person is internal staff or external volunteer.
  3. Add to the correct Microsoft Group membership.
  4. Confirm admin@ remains a member.
  5. Verify Power Automate sends membership-change notification.
  6. Ask the group owner or new member to test delivery, or send a test message yourself.

SOP: Remove a Person from a Committee Mailing List

  1. Confirm removal request and effective date.
  2. Remove member from the Microsoft Group.
  3. Verify Power Automate notification is received.
  4. If person held one of the six officer roles, check related shared mailbox permissions.

SOP: Leadership Transition for Role Inbox

  1. Identify affected role mailbox (e.g., accchair@).
  2. Remove outgoing person's mailbox permissions.
  3. Grant incoming person's mailbox permissions.
  4. Validate that incoming person can open the shared mailbox from their own account.
  5. Keep address and historical content in place for continuity.

SOP: New Committee Creation

  1. Create new Microsoft Group for the committee.
  2. Add initial committee members.
  3. Add admin@ as member for archiving.
  4. Ensure membership-change notifications are active.
  5. Record the group in the committee/group inventory.

Governance Rules

  • Every committee must have exactly one official mailing-list group.
  • Every committee group must include admin@.
  • Shared mailbox addresses represent roles and must not be treated as personal identities.
  • Access to shared role inboxes must be updated promptly on leadership change.
  • Membership changes should be performed by staff owner (Anna) or IT admin only.

Recommended Recordkeeping

Maintain a simple inventory table (in the wiki or internal operations file) with:

  • Committee name
  • Group email address
  • Current chair role mailbox (if applicable)
  • Current permission holders
  • Last membership review date
  • Last updated by
This makes volunteer/staff handoff much easier.

Common Issues and Checks

Person does not receive committee emails

  • Member exists in correct Microsoft Group
  • Email address is correct
  • Sender used the correct group address
  • Recent change triggered notification (confirms update happened)

New officer cannot open role mailbox

  • Shared mailbox permission was granted to the person's licensed account
  • User is opening mailbox from their own account context
  • Predecessor access was removed (to avoid confusion)

Missing archive history

  • admin@ is still a member of the affected group
  • Group delivery settings have not been altered

Handoff Checklist (Staff / Volunteer Transition)

  • Review all committee group memberships for accuracy.
  • Verify all six active officer roles have correct shared mailbox access.
  • Remove stale permissions from former role holders.
  • Confirm admin@ is in every group.
  • Confirm membership-change notification flow is working.
  • Update inventory table and date-stamp the review.

Key Contacts and Ownership

RoleContact
Group membership ownerAnna (staff)
Technical ownerIT admin
Archive mailboxadmin@ (not actively monitored)
If ownership changes, update this section immediately.

Related Resources

  • M365 Email Building Blocks — understand the four email patterns (personal mailbox, shared mailbox, mailing list, alias) and when to use each
  • SOP: New Users, Mailboxes & Groups — step-by-step admin procedures for creating users, shared mailboxes, groups, and aliases
  • Office Onboarding Email Templates — copy-and-send messages for the people who receive new access

pages.html:
SHHA uses four distinct patterns for email addresses in Microsoft 365. Before requesting any new address, understand which pattern fits your need. This page is the reference for anyone planning new committees, roles, or special-purpose addresses.

The Four Patterns at a Glance

PatternWhat it isExampleWhen to use it
Personal mailbox; first.last@sandiahomeowners.org A licensed M365 account owned by one person. Has its own login, calendar, OneDrive, etc. anna.smith@sandiahomeowners.org Office staff and IT admins who need to log in to Microsoft 365 and perform admin tasks. Costs a license.
Shared mailbox; role@sandiahomeowners.org A mailbox tied to a position, not a person. Multiple licensed users can open it from their own account. Retains full email history across holders. president@sandiahomeowners.org; cscchair@sandiahomeowners.org Only one of SHHA's six officer roles: President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, ACC Chair, or CSC Chair. Each officer receives Full Access and Send As through the officer's own licensed account.
Mailing list (Microsoft Group); committee@sandiahomeowners.org A distribution group. Email sent to the address is delivered to every current member — including external guests who have no M365 license. csc@sandiahomeowners.org; shha-all@sandiahomeowners.org Any group of people who need to receive the same email. Most committees have one. No license cost for external members.
Alias; (additional address on an existing mailbox or group) An extra email address that delivers to an existing mailbox or group. Not a separate mailbox — just an alternative address for the same destination. wildfire@sandiahomeowners.org → delivers to the ESC group or a specific shared mailbox One-off or special-purpose addresses (task forces, events, topical inboxes) where you do not need a separate mailbox with its own history. Use when you want a memorable address that maps to something that already exists.

Which Pattern Do I Need?

Walk through these questions when planning a new email address:

  1. Does one specific person need to log in to M365 and perform admin tasks?
    • Yes → Personal mailbox (requires a license; talk to IT admin)
    • No → continue
  2. Does the address need its own persistent inbox that survives personnel changes?
    • Yes → Shared mailbox
    • No → continue
  3. Does the address need to deliver to a group of people?
    • Yes → Mailing list (Microsoft Group)
    • No → continue
  4. Do you just need a convenient address that routes to an existing mailbox or group?
    • Yes → Alias on the appropriate existing mailbox or group
    • No → talk to IT admin to figure out the right approach

Combining Patterns

For a committee or task force, the normal setup is:

WhatPatternTypical result
Committee mailing listMicrosoft GroupOne address that reaches all current members, including external volunteers
Committee documentsSharePoint siteOne group-owned Documents library for the committee record
Friendly alias (optional)Alias on the groupAn additional memorable address that routes to the group
Officer role inbox (only when applicable)Shared mailboxOne of the six officer addresses; never a general chair or task-force mailbox

You generally do not need to create personal mailboxes for volunteers. External volunteers receive group email at their personal addresses (Gmail, Yahoo, etc.) and use SharePoint in a browser.

Archive Rule

Every mailing list (Microsoft Group) must include admin@sandiahomeowners.org as a member. This is the archive account that preserves all committee email for continuity and records. It is not monitored for support.

Cost Summary

PatternLicense cost
Personal mailboxRequires a paid M365 license
Shared mailboxFree (up to 50 GB; no license unless it exceeds the limit)
Mailing list (Group)Free
AliasFree (added to an existing mailbox or group)

Where to Go Next

  • Need to create a new user or shared mailbox? See SOP: New Users, Mailboxes & Groups.
  • Need to tell someone what to do next? Use Office Onboarding Email Templates.
  • Need to add/remove members from an existing group? See the SOPs in M365 Email Groups, Role Inboxes & Responsibilities.
  • Not sure what you need? Email ithelp@sandiahomeowners.org with a description of the goal and IT admin will recommend the right pattern.

This SOP is written for SHHA staff who are comfortable with basic Microsoft admin work and need a reliable step-by-step process for setting up new groups, shared mailboxes, and related addresses.

Start here every time: admin.microsoft.com

Quick Start: What Are You Trying to Set Up?

If you need...Go to this section
A new task-force or committee mailing address that sends to all membersSOP A: Create a Microsoft 365 Group (Mailing List)
A SharePoint document site for a new committee or task forceSOP: Create a Committee SharePoint Site
A shared mailbox for one of the six officer rolesSOP B: Create a Shared Mailbox
A friendly one-off address like wildfire@sandiahomeowners.orgSOP C: Add an Alias
An internal staff account with first.last@sandiahomeowners.org loginSOP D: Add a Licensed User
An external volunteer using Gmail/Yahoo/etc.SOP E: Add an External Guest

Task Force Fast Path (Most Common New Setup)

For a new short-term task force, the normal pattern is:

  1. Create a Microsoft 365 Group for the task-force mailing list.
  2. Add members (including external guests) and always include admin@sandiahomeowners.org.
  3. If the request is for one of the six officer roles, use SOP B for the role mailbox. Ordinary committee chairs and task-force leads do not get shared mailboxes.
  4. Add an optional Alias (for example, wildfire@sandiahomeowners.org) if a friendlier address is useful.
  5. Confirm the Microsoft 365 group-connected SharePoint site exists; do not create a duplicate.
  6. Configure document permissions using SOP: Create a Committee SharePoint Site and send members the Committee SharePoint Guide.
  7. Test email delivery, update the Quick Links directory, and send the New Committee Or Task Force email if this is a new group.

If you only need one address that emails the whole task force, do SOP A only.

SOP A: Create a Microsoft 365 Group (Mailing List)

Use this for: any committee/task-force address that should email all members.

Menu path: admin.microsoft.com → Teams & groups → Active teams & groups → Add a group

Step-by-step

  1. Open admin.microsoft.com and sign in.
  2. In the left menu, click Teams & groups.
  3. Click Active teams & groups.
  4. Click Add a group.
  5. Select Microsoft 365 as the group type, then click Next.
  6. Enter:
    • Name: Full task-force name (example: Wildfire Preparedness Task Force)
    • Description: Short purpose statement
    Click Next.
  7. Add at least one Owner (usually office staff), then click Next.
  8. Set:
    • Group email address (example: wildfiretf → wildfiretf@sandiahomeowners.org)
    • Privacy: usually Private
    • Leave "Create a team for this group" off unless Teams is explicitly needed
    Click Next then Create group.
  9. After the group is created, open the new group and go to its Settings pane.
  10. Required: check Let people outside the organization email this team.
  11. Required: check Send copies of team emails and events to team members' inboxes.
  12. Go to Members → Add members.
  13. Add all task-force members (internal and external as available).
  14. Required: Add admin@sandiahomeowners.org as a member for archive continuity.
  15. Send a test email to the new group address and confirm delivery.
  16. Send the New Committee Or Task Force email after the group, membership, and any SharePoint site are tested.

Test after every change: whenever membership or a group setting changes, test the group again. You can add yourself temporarily, send a test message, and remove yourself afterward. If external delivery matters, you can also add a personal Gmail account temporarily, test it, and remove it when finished.

Done checklist

  • Group exists
  • Owners added
  • All members added
  • External email enabled
  • Inbox delivery enabled
  • admin@ added
  • Test email delivered after setup and after any later change

SOP B: Create a Shared Mailbox (Six Officer Roles Only)

Use this only for: President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, ACC Chair, or CSC Chair. Shared mailboxes are a little fussy to administer, but officer history is important enough that SHHA keeps it this way.

Do not use this for: ordinary committee chairs, task-force leads, external volunteers, or general committee communication. Use the person's own account and the committee Microsoft Group instead.

Menu path: admin.microsoft.com → Teams & groups → Shared mailboxes → Add a shared mailbox

Step-by-step

  1. Confirm the role is one of the six officer roles above. If it is any other chair or lead, stop and use the committee mailing-list procedure.
  2. Click Add a shared mailbox.
  3. Enter the role name and address, such as president@sandiahomeowners.org.
  4. Save the mailbox, then open its details and choose Members → Edit → Add members.
  5. Add the incoming officer's licensed @sandiahomeowners.org account.
  6. Grant that account both Full Access and Send As. These are separate permissions; grant both.
  7. Send the Officer Shared Mailbox Access email with the direct role address and the wiki link.
  8. Ask the officer to sign in to Outlook with their own account and manually add the shared mailbox. It will not appear automatically in every Outlook setup.
  9. Test that the officer can open the mailbox, read an incoming test message, and send with the role address in the From field.
  10. Tell the officer to send official role correspondence from the role mailbox or copy it. The shared mailbox is the role's archive; a personal inbox is not.

Important notes

  • The officer does not log in directly to the shared mailbox. There is no separate shared-mailbox password to give them.
  • For current Outlook instructions, see Open and use a shared mailbox in Outlook.
  • For a change of officer, remove the outgoing officer's permissions, grant the incoming officer both permissions, and test again.

SOP C: Add an Alias (One-Off Friendly Address)

Use this for: addresses like wildfire@sandiahomeowners.org that should route to an existing group or mailbox.

Menu path: admin.microsoft.com → select target group/mailbox → Email aliases / Email address settings

Step-by-step

  1. Decide destination first: should alias route to the group or the shared mailbox?
  2. For group destination:
    • Go to Teams & groups → Active teams & groups.
    • Select the group.
    • Open email settings and add alias address.
  3. For shared mailbox destination:
    • Go to Teams & groups → Shared mailboxes.
    • Select mailbox.
    • Open email settings and add alias address.
  4. Save changes.
  5. Send test email to alias and verify it arrives in the expected destination.

SOP D: Add a New Licensed User (Internal Staff)

Use this for: staff/admin accounts that need a personal Microsoft login (first.last@sandiahomeowners.org).

Menu path: admin.microsoft.com → Users → Active users → Add a user

Step-by-step

  1. Go to Users → Active users → Add a user.
  2. Enter name and username (first.last format).
  3. Generate temporary password and require password change at first sign-in.
  4. Assign correct M365 license.
  5. Finish adding user.
  6. Add user to appropriate groups/shared mailbox access as needed.
  7. Send the New Internal Staff User email after testing the account.

SOP E: Add an External Guest (Volunteer)

Use this for: most volunteers; avoids paid license cost.

Menu path: admin.microsoft.com → Users → Guest users (or Entra invite flow)

Step-by-step

  1. Invite external user with personal email address.
  2. Ask them to accept Microsoft invitation email.
  3. After acceptance, add them to needed Microsoft Groups.
  4. Verify they receive test group email.
  5. Send the New External Volunteer email after testing access.

Send The Onboarding Email

After setup and testing are complete, choose the matching message from Office Onboarding Email Templates. Replace every placeholder and test every link before sending.

Final Validation (Do This Before You Tell the Office Contact Setup Is Complete)

  • Group email tested
  • Shared mailbox tested (if created)
  • Alias tested (if created)
  • admin@ included in group
  • Quick Links directory updated with new addresses
  • Office contact told setup is complete

Where To Go Next

  • M365 Email Building Blocks for choosing the right pattern first
  • M365 Email Groups, Role Inboxes & Responsibilities for governance and handoff rules
  • SOP: Create a Committee SharePoint Site for document-library setup and permissions
  • Quick Links & Directory to keep the address list current

pages.html:
Audience: SHHA office staff and IT administrators. This is not a committee-member task.

Goal: connect an existing committee Microsoft 365 group to its group-owned SharePoint document library, keep site-page administration with office staff, and give committee members read/write access to documents.

Before You Start

Write down these values before opening Microsoft 365:

Committee nameThe full display name
Microsoft 365 groupThe existing group/mailing-list name
Group emailThe committee mailing-list address
Expected site addresshttps://shha.sharepoint.com/sites/[GROUP-NAME]
Office ownersPrimary and backup office/admin accounts

The finished site should be Private. Office staff are Owners / Full Control. Committee members have Contribute access to documents and do not administer the home page.

Step 1: Find The Existing Group-Connected Site

A Microsoft 365 group normally provisions a connected SharePoint team site. If the mailing list already exists, do not begin by creating another site or group.

  1. Try https://shha.sharepoint.com/sites/[GROUP-NAME].
  2. If that does not open, go to admin.microsoft.com → Show all → Admin centers → SharePoint.
  3. Open Sites → Active sites.
  4. Search for both the committee's full name and group name.
  5. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, open Teams & groups → Active teams & groups, select the group, and confirm its type is Microsoft 365.

If the group-connected site appears in Active sites, open it and continue.

If the Microsoft 365 group exists but no connected site can be found: do not create a similarly named standalone site. Recheck that the group is a Microsoft 365 group and search the SharePoint admin center's Active sites by both the group name and the full committee name. If the site is still not listed, record the group name and leave site setup pending until Microsoft finishes provisioning it. A duplicate would separate mailing-list membership from document access.

Step 2: Confirm Office Staff Are Owners

  1. In the SharePoint admin center, open Sites → Active sites.
  2. Select the committee site.
  3. Select Membership.
  4. Confirm the primary and backup office/admin accounts are Owners or site admins.
  5. Add a backup office/admin owner if needed.
  6. Do not make the committee chair or ordinary committee members Owners.

Owners may edit the home page, navigation, permissions, and site settings. Keep that role with office staff.

Step 3: Give Members Document Access Without Site Editing

Microsoft normally gives group-connected team-site members Edit permission. SHHA uses Contribute so members can work with documents without managing lists or editing the site page.

  1. Open the committee SharePoint site.
  2. Select Settings → Site permissions.
  3. Select Advanced permissions settings.
  4. Select the SharePoint group whose name ends in Members. Do not select Owners or Visitors.
  5. Select Edit User Permissions.
  6. Clear Edit.
  7. Select Contribute.
  8. Select OK.

Do not remove the committee Microsoft 365 group from the site. Group membership keeps the mailing list and document access synchronized.

Step 4: Keep The Site Simple

A team site already includes a default Documents library. Do not create a second Documents library.

  1. Open Documents and confirm it works.
  2. Create a folder named Documents Shared with Board.
  3. If folder colors are available, apply the standard SHHA committee-folder color.
  4. Edit the left navigation and remove unused links. Keep the useful experience limited to Home and Documents.
  5. Do not delete the system Site Pages library; it supports the home page.

Step 5: Make The Home Page Minimal

Only office staff should edit the home page.

  1. From the home page, select Edit.
  2. Use the committee's full name as the title.
  3. Add: “Use the Documents library for committee files and enduring reference materials.”
  4. Add or keep an obvious link to Documents.
  5. Remove unnecessary news, activity, and decorative web parts.
  6. Republish the page.

Step 6: Add The Library To Office OneDrive

This is only for internal office users with SHHA Microsoft accounts. External users should never use OneDrive for committee documents; they use SharePoint in their browser.

  1. Sign in as the office user who needs the shortcut.
  2. Open the committee SharePoint site and then Documents.
  3. Select Add shortcut to OneDrive or Add shortcut to My files.
  4. Open that user's OneDrive and confirm the committee folder appears under My files.
  5. If the desktop OneDrive app is used, confirm the shortcut appears on that computer.
  6. Repeat while signed in as each internal office user who needs the shortcut.

The shortcut points to the group-owned SharePoint library. It does not copy files into a personal OneDrive.

Step 7: Test With An External Member

  1. Ask one existing external group member to open the committee SharePoint site using the same personal email address that received the Microsoft invitation.
  2. Confirm the member can open Documents.
  3. Have the member upload a temporary file named TEST - delete me.
  4. Confirm the member can edit, rename, move, and delete the test file.
  5. Confirm the member cannot edit the home page, navigation, permissions, or membership.
  6. Confirm someone outside the group cannot open the private site.
  7. Remind the external tester to bookmark the SharePoint site and not use OneDrive.

Step 8: Publish The Member Instructions

  1. Send members the Committee SharePoint Guide.
  2. Add the committee mailing list and SharePoint URL to Quick Links & Directory.
  3. Tell external members to bookmark the SharePoint site. Do not give them OneDrive instructions.
  4. Send the matching New Committee Or Task Force or New SharePoint Site For An Existing Committee email.

Final Checklist

  • Existing group-connected site found; no duplicate created
  • Site is Private
  • Office staff are Owners / Full Control
  • Committee members use Contribute permissions
  • Documents library works
  • Documents Shared with Board folder created
  • Home page and navigation simplified
  • Office-user OneDrive shortcuts added separately
  • External member document test passed through SharePoint
  • External member cannot edit the site page
  • Directory updated
  • General member guide sent
  • Matching onboarding email sent

Microsoft References

  • Create a team site in SharePoint
  • Manage sites in the SharePoint admin center
  • Permission levels in SharePoint
  • Add shortcuts to shared folders in OneDrive

Who this is for: the incoming IT professional and staff arranging continuity. Start by obtaining approved individual access through the office, then read the maintained repository guides. This public page explains the systems and responsibilities; credentials, recovery codes, private records and detailed security configuration belong in approved private documentation.

Deployment and address checks: October 13, 2026. Read the current repository status and actual cloud settings before acting; names and migration status can change.

Start with ownership and access

  1. Ask office staff to arrange approved access to the SHHA GitHub organization, Azure subscription, Microsoft 365/Entra administration and the relevant DNS/service-provider accounts. Use your own named accounts.
  2. The repositories are in the Sandia Heights Homeowners Association GitHub organization. The office-accessible sandiahomeowners@gmail.com account is an organization owner; coordinate access and account recovery through the office.
  3. Confirm a primary and backup administrator, billing/renewal owners and recovery contacts for each service. GitHub access does not grant Azure, Microsoft or DNS access.
  4. Keep passwords, API tokens, database connection strings, MFA recovery codes and resident/editorial records out of this wiki and public Git history.

Service accounts and sign-in

SHHA's designated Google account for service ownership is sandiahomeowners@gmail.com (also written Sandiahomeowners@gmail.com). Use Continue with Google and select that account for providers that support it and are linked to the existing SHHA account. This ownership and sign-in instruction was confirmed by SHHA on October 16, 2026; successful access to each provider still needs to be recorded in the private handover register. An email address on an account does not by itself prove that Google sign-in is linked.

For day-to-day administration, use approved individual membership where the provider supports it, while retaining SHHA ownership. Microsoft services and BookStack's Microsoft editing login retain their existing Microsoft identities. Do not create a replacement account, move resources or change authentication just to make a login match this list. If the expected account opens an empty dashboard or asks you to sign up, stop and ask IT Help or office staff to identify the existing account.

Service and entry pointWhat SHHA must retainSign-in and handover check
Google account, Gmail, Drive and DocsOrganizational service ownership and the GRIT issue folders, editing templates and production files.Use the designated Google account. Confirm office continuity and access to the current GRIT workspace; keep recovery methods and codes in the approved private register.
NeonGRIT PostgreSQL submissions, settings, captions and photo metadata.Use Google sign-in with the designated account; verify the existing SHHA project and correct database branch. Preserve database backups separately from application source and photo files.
Name.com via VercelDomain registrations and renewals held in SHHA's account.Access Name.com through Vercel using SHHA's existing account. Confirm the actual domain list, renewal responsibility and delegated access privately; do not assume it holds every SHHA domain or hosts its DNS.
CloudflareGRIT Turnstile CAPTCHA and any other configured SHHA services.Use the designated Google account when linked; confirm the existing account and Turnstile widget. Check allowed hostnames. Turnstile use does not establish that Cloudflare hosts SHHA DNS.
ResendGRIT submission confirmations and sender-domain configuration.Use Google sign-in with the designated account; confirm the existing team and sending domain. Provider login and the application's sending API key are separate access paths.
GitHubSource repositories, organization ownership, deployment workflows and the public wiki mirror.The office-accessible designated account is recorded as an organization owner. Verify its actual sign-in method and retain named maintainer access and a backup owner.
Azure and Microsoft 365Application hosting, wiki MySQL/files, GRIT Blob photos, mail, SharePoint and Entra identities.Use authorized Microsoft identities and assigned roles. Google service ownership does not grant subscription or tenant access. Keep the existing Microsoft BookStack login and individual edit attribution.
InMotionThe authoritative association-domain DNS documented in the dated DNS section, plus any website/hosting services in the actual account.Confirm the current account, login method, website maintainer and DNS owner through the office. Record any exception to Google sign-in privately.
VercelThe access route to SHHA's Name.com account, plus the earlier GRIT public host and domain configuration while the Azure cutover remains pending.Check the existing team's account and actual sign-in method. Retain access until public hosting, DNS, TLS and rollback requirements are verified. Include Name.com access in any Vercel retirement review.
DigitalOceanAny remaining legacy hosting, reminder workloads and recovery material awaiting retirement review.Confirm ownership and sign-in through the private migration handover. Do not retire resources or restart legacy senders as part of documenting accounts.
Adobe, QuickBooks, Square and other office subscriptionsGRIT layout licensing and the office's accounting, sales and payment services.Ask office staff for each existing owner, approved login and billing contact. Do not assume that every office subscription uses Google or the same shared identity. See Systems Inventory.

Cloudflare's sign-in documentation describes restrictions on linking Google to an existing account; verify the existing login before making changes. For SHHA's Name.com access, start in Vercel as instructed above. A provider's Google button is not proof that it reaches SHHA's existing resources.

Private account handover register

Maintain the full register in an office-approved private location accessible to the primary and backup administrator independently of this wiki server. For every service, record the account or organization, actual sign-in method and owner, named administrators, billing and renewal responsibility, domains/projects it controls, backup location, and the date access and restoration were last checked. Record a protected credential-vault reference and recovery custodian there; keep passwords, tokens, connection strings, payment details, recovery codes and personal recovery contacts out of this public wiki and Git repository.

During handover, open each existing service with the incoming administrator, confirm the expected resources and permissions, and update the private register. Preserve domain renewal access, Google account recovery, Neon data, Azure photo bytes, wiki database/files/configuration and production assets separately. The public Markdown/HTML mirror preserves readable documentation; it cannot recover those accounts or replace full system backups.

Systems and sources of truth

SystemResponsibility and infrastructureMaintained source
Association website and resident databaseThe website's MariaDB database owns homeowner, property and resident-link records. Authorized website administrators make corrections there. The toolbox and public dashboard use dedicated SELECT-only access; neither is a replacement membership database.Obtain the website maintainer's operating and recovery documentation through the office.
Microsoft 365Owns mailboxes, calendars, committee groups and SharePoint files. Entra supplies Microsoft identity. The toolbox uses Microsoft Graph for calendar/group reads and approved mail delivery; it does not create a second calendar or change group membership.Microsoft administration and the private toolbox connection/operations guide.
SHHA ToolboxNode.js 24 LTS application on Azure App Service. Platform Microsoft authentication verifies identity; the app enforces separate tool grants. Operational configuration, successful-send history, queued work and authorized private review state persist outside deployed application files.SHHA-toolbox, private, deployment branch main.
Public statistics dashboardSeparate Node.js 24 LTS Azure App Service application at dashboard.sandiahomeowners.org. It reads aggregates through SELECT-only queries and generates reports in memory. It has no private staff tools, Graph mail or reminder worker.SHHA-dashboard, private, deployment branch main.
IT wikiUpstream BookStack in an Azure App Service container, with Azure Database for MySQL and persistent Azure Files for configuration/uploads. Public reading and native BookStack Microsoft OIDC editing are separate. Preserve APP_KEY, the database and uploaded files during upgrades or recovery.SHHA-wiki, public. Local project folder: SHHA-wiki. Branch main checks tools and mirrors public content; it does not deploy the BookStack container.
GRIT submissionsThe public site is sandiaheightsgrit.app. Its domain still served the Vercel-hosted version at this check. The Azure migration version uses Next.js/React on Node.js 22 LTS, Neon PostgreSQL, private Azure Blob photo storage, Cloudflare Turnstile and Resend. Public-domain cutover to Azure remains separate from deploying that version.grit-newsletter, private. Use azure for the Azure deployment; main retains earlier source. Read its deployment guide before choosing a branch.
Neighborhood mapMaster mapping work is done in QGIS and exported with qgis2web/OpenLayers. GitHub Pages serves the public web export. Its layers and attribute tables are public; the site does not query the homeowner database. Street tiles use OpenStreetMap; aerial imagery uses USGS. Browser filters do not make any published data private.SHHA-map, public, publication branch main. Back up the master QGIS project and source GIS data separately.

The toolbox, dashboard and Azure newsletter version currently share existing Azure compute, with separate applications, settings and deployments. The wiki uses its own plan, database and file storage. Confirm subscriptions, resources, network configuration and current costs in the protected repository/cloud inventory; a public URL or repository name is not a complete deployment specification.

Current addresses and DNS

  • wiki.sandiahomeowners.org: Azure BookStack; anyone can read, approved Microsoft users can edit.
  • dashboard.sandiahomeowners.org: public aggregate dashboard on Azure.
  • toolbox.sandiahomeowners.org: protected staff toolbox with Microsoft login and per-tool grants.
  • sandiaheightsgrit.app: public contribution site; confirm the migration status before changing its host.
  • Neighborhood map on GitHub Pages: current map address; a map subdomain is deferred.

The standalone reminders web address is retired; its function is in Toolbox → Email Reminders. Older toolbox statistics/Board Report links redirect to the separate public dashboard.

InMotion provides the authoritative DNS zone for sandiahomeowners.org at this check; the GRIT domain uses Vercel nameservers. Registrar, DNS provider and application host are different responsibilities. Moving hosting does not require moving nameservers. Preserve mail and unrelated verification records when changing a web destination. Verify the final HTTPS binding/certificate and Microsoft callback, not just the DNS record.

Microsoft login and permission boundaries

The toolbox uses Azure App Service Authentication and its independent group/user grants. A Microsoft sign-in or committee membership does not automatically grant resident-data access. Invited guests can use their own personal email identity in the SHHA tenant without an SHHA email suffix.

BookStack uses its own native OIDC registration and page/role permissions. Do not apply toolbox authentication rules to the wiki: public reading must remain available while edits stay attributed to signed-in people. The GRIT editor uses its own protected editorial access rather than toolbox Microsoft grants.

Retain the existing shared Entra application used by the toolbox and Microsoft Graph when retiring legacy reminder code; an older application name is not evidence it can be deleted. Keep the master calendar/sender admin@sandiahomeowners.org. SHHA display and reminder timezone is America/Denver.

Development, deployment and documentation

  1. Read the project's README, AGENTS.md, deployment and operations guides. Verify the actual deployment branch. Inspect Git status and recent commits; other IT work may share a checkout. Preserve unfinished drafts and do not publish them accidentally.
  2. For Node applications, use the project's declared Node LTS version and committed lockfile. Test with synthetic data. Toolbox/dashboard changes go through their checks and exact Azure deployment; newsletter changes use the Azure branch workflow. A healthy endpoint alone does not verify database, photo, CAPTCHA or email integrations.
  3. For the map, edit the master QGIS source, export outside the repository, use the approved importer, review public fields, then verify GitHub Pages deployment. The website export is not the master GIS backup.
  4. For wiki content, edit the live WYSIWYG page or deliberately send current HTML through BookStack's API. Pull before changing a page, preserve newer human edits and verify live readback. Do not round-trip converted Markdown over rich tables.
  5. The wiki's nightly/on-demand GitHub job exports anonymous public pages as Markdown, rendered HTML and metadata. It makes no BookStack writes and needs no administrator token. Restricted content is omitted from new exports, but previously public content remains in Git history. Maintain private content backups separately.
  6. BookStack software upgrades are separate from content sync. Review the pinned upstream container release, take compatible database/file/configuration backups and plan rollback before applying schema-changing upgrades. Azure deployment CI/CD for the wiki remains work to finish.

Operations and recovery

Azure's current toolbox settings enable email sending, reminder scheduling, group monitoring and group notifications. An authorized administrator should verify Operational status and recent delivery history before relying on a rule or changing automation. This settings check is not a test email or proof that every delivery path works.

The retired reminders address does not establish whether every old hosting workload or scheduler has been shut down. Confirm final state import, successful-send history, the prior scheduler's shutdown and rollback arrangements in the private migration runbook before calling that operational cutover complete. Do not restore an old sending service alongside the current worker.

  • Toolbox deployments must preserve persistent state, send deduplication history, reminder rules, group baselines, queued notices and access policy. Read its private backup rules: some authorized review/campaign files need separate handling rather than entering routine operational backups.
  • Wiki recovery needs MySQL data, configuration/APP_KEY and uploaded-file storage. Markdown/HTML or a portable content ZIP is not a complete installation backup. Full recovery testing remains to be completed.
  • GRIT recovery must cover both Neon records and photo bytes. The current public site and Azure preview share live data; use a separate development database for routine testing. Read the repository's approved migration/integration procedures.
  • Keep an independent recovery copy, document responsible people and test restoration. Confirm master GIS backups, DNS/domain renewals and cloud certificate renewal.

First tasks for the incoming IT professional

  1. Confirm office-assisted access, ownership, backup administrators and service billing/renewal contacts.
  2. Recheck live URLs, private repository guides, deployment branches and cloud settings. Resolve discrepancies between older migration notes and current operation.
  3. Review page visibility and repository visibility together before adding sensitive material. The wiki and its public mirror are not a place for private infrastructure inventories or security-remediation details.
  4. Verify recovery coverage and remaining cutovers, including the GRIT public domain, wiki platform deployment workflow and legacy hosting retirement.
  5. Update this overview with verified completion dates; keep passwords, tenant/resource identifiers, permissions inventories and recovery instructions in the approved private runbooks.

See Public Utilities and SHHA Toolbox for the reader-facing guide and Systems Inventory for the wider software/service list.

Who this is for: staff, volunteers and IT administrators using SHHA accounts and documents. For an access problem or a suspicious sign-in prompt, contact IT Help.

Use the right account

  1. Use the same email address that received your SHHA invitation for guest access. Staff and officer mailbox holders use their own SHHA account for licensed services.
  2. Open committee documents from the committee SharePoint site. Access comes from approved group membership; a public wiki link does not grant access.
  3. Open a shared role mailbox through your own licensed account. Do not sign in as the shared role address.

Keep private information in protected systems

This wiki and its GitHub content mirror are public. Do not add passwords, API tokens, recovery codes, resident records, private reports or detailed permissions inventories. A later page restriction does not remove material already saved in public Git history.

Use the correct committee or staff document library for working files. If you are unsure who should see a file, ask office staff before uploading or sharing it.

Request or remove access

  1. Ask office staff for committee membership changes and provide the person's email address, committee and effective date.
  2. Ask IT Help for shared-mailbox permissions or technical access problems.
  3. After a change, test the affected email or document access. Keep the role mailbox and group-owned documents for the next person; change access rather than deleting the records.

If something looks suspicious

Do not enter a password or approve a sign-in request you did not initiate. Contact IT Help using the address on this page. Describe what happened and include the affected account and time; do not email passwords or one-time codes.

Backups and recovery

The public wiki export is a readable content copy. Restoring BookStack also requires its database, configuration and uploaded files. Other services have their own recovery procedures. IT maintainers should obtain the approved private operating guides and confirm restoration coverage; cloud hosting alone does not demonstrate a tested recovery process.
